benefits-geo-and-source-ip.statement: Private Service Edges typically benefit organizations that have geopolitical requirements or that use applications requiring the organization's IP address as the source IP address.

quotes: Private Service Edges typically benefit organizations that have certain geopolitical requirements or those that use applications that require an organization's IP address as the source IP address.

deployable-criteria.statement: Zscaler can deploy Private Service Edges in locations with geopolitical requirements and regulations, locations with high latency to Public Service Edges, applications that require the organization's IP address as the source IP, users who need localized content, or where overall upload throughput is beyond 1 Gbps or download throughput is beyond 2 Gbps. Lower bandwidths can be considered as exceptions.

quotes: Zscaler can deploy Private Service Edges in locations that meet the following requirements:
Locations with certain geopolitical requirements and regulations.
Locations that experience high latency when connecting to Public Service Edges.
Users who need to see localized content.
Organizations and locations where the overall upload throughput traffic is beyond 1 Gbps or download throughput traffic is beyond 2 Gbps.
Lower bandwidths can be considered as exceptions.
Applications that require an organization's IP address as the source IP address.

comparison-pse.statement: In the vendor's Private versus Virtual Service Edge comparison, the Private Service Edge is a good choice for high throughput, especially when the overall uplink throughput traffic is above 1 Gbps; it supports remote user traffic and has inbuilt SSL inspection, at least two are required for redundancy, Cloud Operations configures, maintains and monitors it, and Zscaler provides the hardware and software. The page refers the choice to the Zscaler Account team.

quotes: Good choice for high throughput, especially when the overall uplink throughput traffic is above 1 Gbps.
Support remote user traffic. Have the inbuilt ability to perform SSL inspection.
You must have at least two Private Service Edges for redundancy.
Cloud Operations configures, maintains, and monitors the Private Service Edge.
Zscaler provides hardware and software for Private Service Edge.
For more information on the right choice for your deployment, contact your Zscaler Account team.

recommend-above-1gbps-download.statement: For more than 1 Gbps of download throughput, Zscaler recommends deploying Private Service Edges.

quotes: For more than 1 Gbps of download throughput, Zscaler recommends deploying Private Service Edges.

uplink-or-download.summary: Whether the 1 Gbps Private Service Edge threshold is on download or on overall uplink throughput.

quotes: For more than 1 Gbps of download throughput, Zscaler recommends deploying Private Service Edges.

positions.says: The understanding article recommends Private Service Edges for more than 1 Gbps of download throughput.

quotes: Good choice for high throughput, especially when the overall uplink throughput traffic is above 1 Gbps.

positions.says: The comparison page calls the Private Service Edge a good choice for high throughput, especially when overall uplink throughput traffic is above 1 Gbps.

uplink-or-download.impact: The same 1 Gbps figure is attached to download on one page and to overall uplink on the other, so it cannot be applied to a link without knowing which is meant; see also the open threshold-wording gap.

threshold-wording.title: Which throughput threshold qualifies a location for a PSE
threshold-wording.detail: The page gives two thresholds that do not line up: a recommendation to deploy above 1 Gbps of download, and a deployable-locations criterion of upload beyond 1 Gbps or download beyond 2 Gbps. With the page's own 30% upload assumption, 1 Gbps of upload would correspond to about 3.3 Gbps of download, so the criterion reads as if upload and download were swapped. Unverified legacy statement (corrected here): the legacy doc wrote the threshold as 'download over about 1 Gbps / total over about 2 Gbps' and called it the Public Service Edge threshold. Zscaler Sales or Support would settle which wording is intended.
